settings.title: Settings
settings.fontFamilyDesc: The font used in the editor.
settings.bookSpacingDesc: Adds extra vertical space between lines for a book-like reading experience.
settings.typewriterScrollDesc: Keeps the active line at a fixed vertical position so you don't write near the bottom of the page.
settings.pageViewDesc: Renders the editor as a printed-book-style page with paper background, margins, and shadow.
settings.bookWidthDesc: Constrains the editor width to match a printed book page, so line breaks approximate the final output.
settings.bookWidthCustomDesc: Width of the text area in inches.
settings.uiLanguageDesc: Language used for the application interface.
settings.accentColorDesc: Primary highlight color used throughout the interface.
settings.customAssetsHint: Themes and interface languages can also be dropped into folders on disk. Novalist reads them when it starts, so restart after adding a file.
settings.scopeEditingGlobal: Editing your global defaults. This project follows them.
settings.scopeEditingProject: Editing this project only. Your global defaults are unchanged.
settings.scopeProjectHint: When on, this section's values are saved with the project (in its .novalist folder) and override your global settings. Open a project to enable.
settings.goalsDesc: These goals drive the status bar progress indicators for the active project.
settings.dailyWordGoalDesc: Target number of new words to write per day.
settings.projectWordGoalDesc: Target total word count for the full project.
settings.projectAuthorDesc: Author name used as default on the dashboard header and in exports.
settings.quoteStyleDesc: Selects the language preset for smart quotes, em-dashes, and ellipsis replacement.
settings.dialogueCorrectionDesc: Automatically corrects comma and period placement around quotation marks in dialogue, based on the selected quote style language.
settings.grammarCheckDesc: Checks your text for grammar, spelling, and style issues using LanguageTool. Requires an internet connection (or a self-hosted LanguageTool server).
settings.grammarCheckApiUrlDesc: Endpoint used for grammar checks. Leave blank to use the free public API. Point at a self-hosted LanguageTool server (for example http://localhost:8081/v2/check) to keep your text local.
settings.grammarCheckUsernameDesc: The email address associated with your LanguageTool Premium account. Leave blank for the free public API.
settings.grammarCheckApiKeyDesc: Your LanguageTool access token for Premium features. Stored in settings; do not share.
settings.grammarCheckCredentialsInvalid: ✗ Invalid email, API key, or server unreachable
settings.grammarCheckPickyModeDesc: Enables additional creative writing style, tone, and formatting rules.
settings.grammarCheckMotherTongueDesc: Enables LanguageTool's false-friends rules to check for native language interference (e.g. Germanisms).
settings.aiEnabledDesc: Connect to an AI provider for AI-powered analysis and chat.
settings.aiApiTokenDesc: Optional bearer token for LM Studio authentication.
settings.aiCopilotPathDesc: Path to the GitHub Copilot CLI executable. Use 'copilot' if it is on your PATH.
settings.aiSystemPromptDesc: Custom system prompt sent to the AI. Leave empty to use the default prompt. Use {{LANGUAGE}} as a placeholder for the current UI language.
settings.checkForExtensionUpdatesDesc: Automatically check for extension updates on startup
settings.githubTokenDesc: Optional token to increase API rate limits when browsing or updating extensions (60/hr → 5000/hr)
settings.diagnosticLoggingDesc: Write a technical log to a file you can send for support. It records only app events, settings, and errors — never your story text, characters, locations, scenes, or file names. You can open and read the file before sending it.
settings.spellCheckHint: Uses the system spell checker, so it works with no network and nothing you write leaves the machine. Right-click a red-underlined word for corrections, or to teach it the word.
settings.spellCheckLanguagesHint: Leave all unticked to follow your writing language. A dictionary is downloaded once the first time you use it, then works offline.
settings.spellCheckDictionaryHint: Words you told Novalist to accept. They travel with your settings.
settings.spellCheckDictionaryEmpty: No words added yet. Right-click a red-underlined word in your prose to add one.
settings.composeDimmingDesc: Everything but the paragraph your caret is in fades back. Takes effect in the editor, and is most useful with focus mode (Alt+F), which now hides the toolbar and status bar as well as the side panes.

project.description: Walks you from a one-line premise to an outlined manuscript with seed cast.

projectName.title: What's the project called?
projectName.help: The display name for the project; also the folder name on disk.

bookName.title: Working title of the first book

premise.title: Premise — one sentence
premise.help: What is your story about in a single line? Try the form: A [character] wants [goal] but [obstacle].
premise.placeholder: A retired thief must rob the man who framed her.

paragraph.title: Expand the premise into a paragraph
paragraph.help: Set up the world, stakes, the inciting incident, and the rough shape of the climax.

actOne.title: Act 1 — Setup
actOne.help: What's the status quo? Who's the protagonist before they're forced to change?

actTwo.title: Act 2 — Confrontation
actTwo.help: The middle. Rising tension, complications, the protagonist tries and fails.

actThree.title: Act 3 — Resolution
actThree.help: Climax + new equilibrium. What's the cost? What changed?

chaptersPerAct.title: Roughly how many chapters per act?
chaptersPerAct.help: We'll create placeholder chapters under each act. Aim for 5–12. You can add and remove chapters freely later.

protagonists.title: Who is this story about? (protagonists)
protagonists.help: Add one or more main characters. Just names for now — develop them later in the Codex.

antagonists.title: Who stands in the way? (antagonists)
antagonists.help: Add the people, factions, or forces opposing the protagonist.

interview.description: Walks the seven psychology pillars: wound, fear, lie, want, need, secret, voice.

name.title: Name
name.help: The character's primary name. You can add aliases later.

wound.title: Wound
wound.help: A formative event from the character's past that still shapes them. Often the source of the lie they believe.

fear.title: Fear
fear.help: What does the character most fear happening to them? It's often a re-occurrence of the wound.

lie.title: Lie they believe
lie.help: The false belief about themselves or the world the character has internalised — "I'm unlovable", "strength = isolation", "the world is fair".

want.title: Want (external goal)
want.help: The thing the character is consciously chasing. Tangible, in-world, can be pointed at.

need.title: Need (internal truth)
need.help: The lesson they must learn — usually the inverse of the lie. Often realised in act three.

secret.title: Secret
secret.help: Something the character hides from other characters (and maybe themselves).

voice.title: Voice — sample lines
voice.help: A few sentences in this character's voice so their dialogue stays consistent across the manuscript.

character.surnameHelp: Family name. Leave blank if not applicable.
character.ageHelp: A literal value (e.g. "23") or descriptor (e.g. "early 30s"). Date-based ages can be set on the entity afterwards.
character.groupHelp: Family, organisation, faction — free text, used to cluster the cast.
character.descriptionHelp: A one-paragraph thumbnail — surfaces in the focus peek.

location.parentHelp: If this place sits inside another (e.g. a city inside a country).

item.originHelp: Where the item came from in-world.

map.pinEntityWatermark: Type to search characters, locations, items, lore…
map.layerAddChildTooltip: Add a child layer nested under this one.
map.isolateTooltip: Show only this image in the view so you can see what you are editing. View-only — not saved.
map.layerDeleteMessage: Delete layer "{0}" and all its images? This cannot be undone.
map.layerZoomRangeCaption: Visible zoom range — 0 = no limit on that side. Example: From=5 hides the layer until you zoom in past 5x.
map.floorMode: Floor mode (one layer at a time)
map.floorModeTooltip: Treat layers as stacked floors of a building. Only the active floor renders; others stay hidden until selected. Useful for multi-level maps where you don't want bleed-through.
map.editClipTooltip: Toggle clip-mask editing on the selected image. Drag points to reshape, double-click image to add, right-click a point to remove. Esc cancels, Enter saves.
map.toolAddImageTooltip: Add an image to the active layer.
map.toolAddPinTooltip: Pin place mode — click anywhere on the map to place a pin. Esc to cancel.
map.toolAddLabelTooltip: Label mode — click anywhere on the map to drop a text label and start typing. Esc to cancel.
map.toolZoomFitTooltip: Zoom to fit — frame all visible images.
map.toolSplineTooltip: Draw roads & rivers — pick a type, then click to lay down points. Enter finishes, Esc cancels.
map.profileBandsHint: from / to are half-width fractions: 0 = centreline, ±1 = road edge. Stack bands to build a sidewalk | curb | lanes | median cross-section.
map.splineBlend: Type-blend smoothing (0 = hard cut, 1 = full blend)
map.emptyState: No map selected. Create one on the left to get started.
map.clipHint: Drag points · Double-click image to add · Right-click point to remove · Esc to cancel
map.splineEditHint: Drag knots to move · drag outer dot for width · right-click knot to remove · Esc / Enter to finish
map.rotHandleTip: Drag to set the spline direction through this knot
map.toolTerrainTooltip: Draw terrain shapes — pick a type, then click to lay down polygon points. Enter finishes, Esc cancels.
map.terrainEditHint: Drag vertices to move · double-click the shape to add a vertex · right-click a vertex to remove · Esc / Done to finish
map.toolBuildingTooltip: Place buildings — pick a type, then click to drop. R re-rolls a new random shape, click keeps placing, Esc exits. Buildings snap to nearby roads; hold Shift to place freely.
map.bldRotateTip: Drag to rotate the building (Shift = 15° steps)
map.fpHint: Wall: click points to chain walls (Enter/Esc ends). Door/Window: click a wall or the outline. Stairs: click start then end. Right-click an element to edit or remove it.
map.fpNoFloorsWarn: Building has no floors. Add a floor first.
map.borderEditHint: Drag vertices to move · double-click the outline to add a vertex · right-click a vertex to remove · Esc / Done to finish
map.bbIdleHint: Click an element to edit. Use the ribbon to add new ones.
map.bbBuildingHint: Click to place. Shift = free angle. Right-drag + wheel = rotate.
map.bbBuildingEditHint: Drag handle to rotate. Use side panel for properties.
map.bbSelectedHint: Drag to move. Right-click for options. Delete to remove.
map.toolBorderTooltip: Map border — draw a clip boundary; everything outside it is hidden. Click again to edit an existing border.
map.exportImageHint: Save the map as a PNG, exactly as it looks here.
map.exportScaleHint: Higher scales give a larger image, for print or endpapers.

backup.title: Backups
backup.enabledDesc: Archives the whole project folder to a ZIP outside the project, so a folder loss or a bad sync cannot take the backups with it. The .git folder is skipped because it is already version control.
backup.intervalDesc: While the project stays open. Set to 0 to back up only on open and close. Values below 5 are treated as 5.
backup.retentionDesc: Older archives are deleted once this many exist. The oldest goes first.
backup.folderDesc: Leave empty for the default location. Choose a synced or external drive to survive losing the machine.
backup.restoreConfirm: Restore the project from the backup taken {{date}}? The current state is archived first, so this can be undone.
backup.noProject: Open a project to see and create its backups.

style.title: Style report
style.description: Craft checks computed offline from your text. Same manuscript, same numbers, every time — nothing is sent anywhere and no AI is involved. These are prompts to look again, not rules.
style.noChapters: Add a chapter to get a report.
style.variationHint: Standard deviation of sentence length. A low number over a long stretch reads as monotonous.

reportDesc.adverbs: Words ending in an adverb suffix. Often a sign the verb is doing too little on its own.
reportDesc.filterWords: Verbs that put the narrator between the reader and the scene: "she saw the door open" rather than "the door opened".
reportDesc.weakVerbs: Verbs that usually have a more specific alternative.
reportDesc.passiveVoice: An auxiliary followed by a participle. Deliberately conservative, so it misses some rather than flagging prose that is fine.
reportDesc.cliches: Stock phrases matched literally against a bundled list.
reportDesc.stickySentences: Sentences where function words crowd out the images.
reportDesc.repeatedOpeners: Three or more sentences in a row opening on the same word.

style.watchWordsDesc: Words you want counted in the style report - your own crutches ("suddenly", "just"), or the spelling a series bible fixes. One per line. They are reported as their own row, separately from Novalist’s bundled checks, and follow you from book to book.

review.title: Import an editor's changes
review.openHint: Read comments and tracked changes from a Word file an editor sent back.
review.description: Novalist reads the comments and tracked changes out of a .docx. Comments can be attached to the open scene. Tracked changes are listed for you to work through rather than applied automatically — an automatic edit to your prose from a file Novalist did not lay out is worse than a list.
review.nothingFound: No comments or tracked changes in that file.
review.revisionsHint: Shown for reference. Make the edits yourself in the scene.
review.applyComments: Add comments to the open scene
review.needsOpenScene: Open a scene to attach comments to it.

matter.description: The pages around your story. Each kind is set its own way in an export, so a dedication is not typeset like a chapter.
matter.heading: Heading
matter.inToc: List in the table of contents
matter.deleteConfirm: Delete this page? Its text is lost.

calendarConfig.title: Calendar setup
calendarConfig.useCustomDesc: Off keeps the Gregorian calendar. On lets you define your own months, month lengths and weekday names, so story durations are counted in your world's time rather than forced into real months and a seven-day week.
calendarConfig.yearLabelDesc: Printed after a year. Leave empty for none.
calendarConfig.dateFormatHint: Write in-world dates as year.month.day — for example 812.3.14 for the 14th day of the third month of year 812.
calendarConfig.erasDesc: Named stretches of years. A date takes the latest era that starts at or before it, so a story spanning a change of reckoning reads correctly on both sides of it. Leave this empty to use the single year label above throughout.
calendarConfig.eraNamePlaceholder: AC, Fourth Age, Before the Fall

manuscriptImport.title: Import a manuscript
manuscriptImport.description: Bring an existing book into this project from Word (.docx), OpenDocument (.odt), EPUB, Markdown, plain text or RTF. Novalist reads the file, works out where the chapters and scenes are, and shows you the plan before writing anything.
manuscriptImport.nothingFound: Nothing could be read from that file. It may be an unsupported format or empty.
manuscriptImport.summary: Found {{chapters}} chapters, {{scenes}} scenes and {{words}} words in this {{format}} file.
manuscriptImport.appendHint: Chapters are added to the end of the book. Nothing already in it is replaced.
manuscriptImport.losses: Not brought across: {{items}}. Novalist has no equivalent for these, so they stay in Scrivener.

match.title: How this name is detected in prose
match.caseSensitiveDesc: For a name that is also an ordinary word: “Will” the character, not “she will go”.
match.matchPluralsDesc: Recognises “Ravens” for an entry called “Raven”. Usually right for a faction or a species, wrong for a person.
match.exclusionsDesc: A detection is skipped when the surrounding text contains one of these — “Rose” the character, excluded from “rose garden”.
match.ignoredScenes: Scenes where this is never detected
match.ignoreHere: Stop detecting this entry in this scene

bulk.confirmArchive: Archive {{count}} scenes? They can be restored from the archive.
bulk.confirmDelete: Delete {{count}} scenes? This cannot be undone.

languagePacks.title: Language packs
languagePacks.intro: Novalist bundles three interface languages and three scene-analysis lexicons. Any other language is a file you or a contributor drops into these folders — no restart needed, just press Rescan.
languagePacks.startLexicon: Start a lexicon for this language
languagePacks.templateWritten: A starting lexicon for {{code}} was written to the analysis folder. Translate the word lists in it, then press Rescan.
languagePacks.lexiconHint: Without a scene-analysis lexicon, a language still writes and exports normally — what it loses is automatic POV, emotion, intensity, conflict and tag detection, and verb-based dialogue attribution. You can set those by hand on any scene.
languagePacks.rescanned: Rescanned. New themes, languages and lexicons are available now.

conflict.title: This scene changed somewhere else
conflict.explain: Your copy and the one on disk both changed, in {{count}} places. Nothing has been saved yet. Pick the version you want for each line — Novalist will not merge your prose for you, because a sentence spliced from two drafts reads like neither.
conflict.snapshotNote: Both versions are snapshotted before this is saved, so you can go back to either one.

aiPolicy.title: What AI may see of this entry
aiPolicy.inclusion: Send this entry to an AI model
aiPolicy.WhenMentionedDesc: The default. The entry goes along when the scene names it, and stays out otherwise.
aiPolicy.AlwaysDesc: Sent with every scene, mentioned or not. For the handful of things a model needs to know about your world constantly.
aiPolicy.NeverDesc: Kept out of anything sent to a model, however relevant it looks. For an unrevealed twist, or for anything you simply do not want a model to see.
aiPolicy.sectionsDesc: Tick a section to keep it back while the rest of the entry still goes. This is how one secret stays hidden without hiding the character it belongs to.

stages.title: Scene stages
stages.intro: The revision states your scenes can be at. Novalist starts you with five that mirror the chapter statuses; rename them, recolour them, or replace them with your own. A stage shows as a coloured dot beside the scene in the binder, and the Dashboard breaks the book down by stage.
stages.countsAsWrittenHint: Words in scenes at this stage count towards your totals. Turn it off for a stage that holds notes rather than prose — an outline placeholder counted as progress inflates every number you use to judge whether you are on track.
stages.unsaved: Unsaved changes. Removing a stage clears it from every scene that was at it.

targets.dashboardHint: A word count to aim for on one scene, one chapter or a whole act. Set one here, or right-click any row in the binder.

publishing.title: Publishing metadata
publishing.intro: What a shop, a library and a distributor need to know about this book, beyond its title and author. All of it is optional — anything you leave blank is simply not written into the exported file.
publishing.isbnUnusable: That is not a usable ISBN — an ISBN is 10 or 13 digits. Nothing will be written until it is.
publishing.seriesHint: A trilogy that does not state its position shelves as three unrelated books. Use 2.5 for a novella between two books.
publishing.subjectsHint: Comma-separated. Genre words, or BISAC codes if you have them — shops use these to shelve the book.

structure.title: Structure
structure.pickOne: Pick a story structure and every one of its beats appears here, ready to be pointed at the scene that fulfils it.
structure.onTarget: Lands at {{actual}}% - about where it should.
structure.name: Name

stateOverride.title: How this changes through the story
stateOverride.intro: Restate this entry at a point in the story - a city razed in act two, an artefact that changes hands, a faction that falls. Anything you leave blank keeps reading from the entry itself. The Codex and the hover card show the restated version when you are reading that part of the book.
stateOverride.descriptionPlaceholder: What it is like, from here

layout.title: Export layouts
layout.builtInHint: This is one of the four layouts Novalist ships, so it cannot be edited — a layout named after a submission standard should keep meaning that standard. Duplicate it and change the copy.
layout.name: Name
layout.chapterTitleFormatHint: Use {{number}} and {{title}}. "Chapter {{number}}: {{title}}" gives "Chapter 3: The Fall"; the default is the title alone.
layout.showSceneTitlesHint: Off for a novel, where the separator is the whole break. On for a collection, or a draft you are sending to someone who needs to name the scenes back to you.
layout.ebookCssHint: Appended to the EPUB stylesheet, so your rules win over Novalist’s. The one place you can reach the look of the ebook itself rather than the page.

analytics.povTitle: Point of view across the book
analytics.unusedTitle: In the Codex, never in the manuscript
analytics.unusedHint: {{names}}. Either they are still to come, or they were planned and quietly dropped.

sprint.title: Writing sprint
sprint.summary: {{count}} sprints, {{words}} words, {{wpm}} words per minute on average.

props.title: Scene and chapter fields
props.intro: Fields of your own on every scene or chapter of this book - tension, a revision pass, a note to yourself. Typed, so a number sorts as a number and a choice stays one of your choices. Scene fields can be shown as a column in the Manuscript outliner.
props.showInOutliner: Show as a column in the outliner
props.unsaved: Unsaved changes. Removing a field also removes what you filled in for it.
props.none: No fields defined for this book yet.

premise.title: Premise
premise.intro: The book in one line, then in one paragraph, then act by act. Written before the chapters and worth re-reading when a scene stops knowing what it is for.
premise.loglinePlaceholder: A retired thief must rob the man who framed her.
premise.paragraphPlaceholder: The world, the stakes, what starts it, and roughly how it ends.

premise.setupIntro: The Snowflake method, briefly: say what the book is in a sentence, open that into a paragraph, then say what happens in each act. You can change all of it later, and skip any of it now.
premise.actHelpOne: The status quo, and who the protagonist is before anything forces them to change.
premise.actHelpTwo: Rising trouble. What they try, and how it fails.
premise.actHelpThree: The climax and what it costs. What is different afterwards.

arc.title: Arc
arc.intro: Where this character starts, where they end, and the scenes that turn them. The per-chapter overrides say what they are like at a point in the book; this says what the change is for.
arc.startPlaceholder: Who they are before anything forces them to change

arc.dashboardIntro: Each character’s turning points in reading order. Turns bunched into one stretch of the book are worth a second look.

labels.title: Scene labels
labels.intro: Labels a scene in this book can carry - "needs a beta read", "cut but keeping", one per thread. Each has a name and a colour, and the colour appears on the scene’s corkboard card. Removing a label takes it off the scenes carrying it.

tension.title: Tension
tension.intro: Each scene’s intensity in reading order. A long flat run, or a peak in the wrong place, is visible here and nowhere else. Click a bar to open that scene.

unlinked.title: Unlinked names
unlinked.intro: Codex names your prose uses as plain text. Novalist recognises them for the Wiki and the hover card, but only a real mention counts towards appearances and co-appearance figures - so an imported or hand-typed manuscript under-reports every one of them. Linking rewrites just that name in that scene.
unlinked.none: Every Codex name in your prose is already linked.
unlinked.link: Link every occurrence in this scene
